_comment: 🧩️ This plugin's contribution to the repository test platform. The framework discovers this file by convention (`testContributionDirName` in 🔣️taxonomy.json) and never names this plugin or any format it owns. Everything format-specific — which reference libraries are approved, what their projections mean, and which native crate carries them — lives here, with the owner of the formats.

oracles.rationale: Typed, step-by-step PDF writer with explicit control over catalog, page tree, media boxes and content streams — the creation reference. Deterministic given the same call sequence, no network, no system dependencies, runs on Windows/macOS/Linux.

PDF document-manipulation library exposing object-level editing, page insert/delete, content-stream rewriting and an independent parser — serves both as the editing oracle and as the independent reader that proves a subject's output is parseable.

The reference PNG encoder/decoder of the Rust ecosystem, and an INDEPENDENT reader for this repository's own encoder. Deterministic for a fixed colour type, bit depth and filter setting, no network, no system dependencies, cross-platform. Scoped to the normative surface: dimensions, colour model, bit depth and decoded samples — filter selection, interlacing and ancillary chunks are encoder freedom and are canonicalized away by semantic-raster-v1.

productionDebt.plan: The OS host rasterizes SVG to PNG through this crate, so it is production-reachable TODAY. Discovered by the oracle-purity gate when png was registered — the gate did its job. Phase 7 target: the rasterizer's PNG writing belongs behind ✏️s/🔌️plugins/🗄️stdio's own encode_png, at which point this entry loses its productionDebt and testOnly becomes a fact.

oracles.rationale: The reference GIF encoder/decoder of the Rust ecosystem. GIF is palette-based, so exact RGBA is a quantizer choice; the oracle is used only for frame geometry, frame count and opaque-sample structure, which the format does fix.

The reference ZIP reader/writer of the Rust ecosystem, and an independent reader for this repository's own writer. Entry order, compression method and level, timestamps and external attributes are writer freedom; member names, uncompressed sizes and content digests are normative and are what semantic-archive-v1 compares.

productionDebt.plan: The OS host declares an optional `zip` dependency for container handling, so it is production-reachable TODAY. Phase 7 target: route that through ✏️s/🔌️plugins/🗄️stdio's own encode_zip/decode_zip.

oracles.rationale: The reference zlib/deflate implementation of the Rust ecosystem. RFC 1951 does not fix WHICH encoding a compressor chooses, so this oracle is deliberately used for the ROUND TRIP — an independent inflater must recover exactly what this repository deflated — never for byte equality.

The reference RIFF/PCM WAVE reader/writer of the Rust ecosystem, and an independent reader for this repository's own writer. Chunk padding, LIST/INFO metadata and chunk order are writer freedom; the format block and the decoded samples are normative.
The reference RFC 4180 CSV reader/writer of the Rust ecosystem. Line terminator, quote style and trailing newline are writer freedom; the header and the cell grid are normative.

The reference BMP encoder/decoder of the Rust ecosystem, and an INDEPENDENT reader for this repository's own encoder. One crate covers BMP, TIFF and JPEG, so a single approved dependency serves three formats rather than three. Scoped to the normative surface: dimensions, colour model and the decoded samples. BMP carries no alpha channel, so the reference is given RGB and the projection compares what a conforming reader recovers, never a channel the format cannot hold.

productionDebt.plan: The `image` crate is production-reachable TODAY from two places: the 🎞️animate plugin's video engine and 🧰️framework/🔨️modules/🗺️surface's tiled-map. Discovered by the oracle-purity gate the moment `image` was registered — the gate did its job. Phase 7 target: both call sites want raster decode/encode that ✏️s/🔌️plugins/🗄️stdio already implements, so routing them through decode_bmp / decode_tiff / decode_jpg retires the dependency and this record with it.

oracles.rationale: The reference TIFF encoder/decoder of the Rust ecosystem, and an independent reader for this repository's own encoder. TIFF leaves compression scheme, strip layout, byte order and ancillary tags to the writer; dimensions, colour model and decoded samples are normative and are what semantic-raster-v1 compares.

oracles.rationale: The reference JPEG encoder/decoder of the Rust ecosystem. JPEG is LOSSY, so this oracle is deliberately NOT used for sample equality: the projection reports geometry and a coarse luma histogram, which is what the codec actually preserves. Asserting exact pixels through a lossy codec would be a test that can only pass by accident.

oracles.rationale: The reference Wavefront OBJ reader of the Rust ecosystem. OBJ has no reference WRITER — it is a plain-text grammar — so the oracle writes the grammar directly and tobj serves as the independent reader that makes the comparison meaningful. Whitespace, numeric formatting and statement order are writer freedom; the vertex set, face topology and counts are normative.

The reference binary/ASCII STL reader and writer of the Rust ecosystem. STL is a triangle soup with no vertex index and a derivable per-facet normal, so the projection compares resolved corner positions per triangle — what the format actually fixes — rather than an index buffer the format never had.

comparisonProfiles.description: PDF documents compared by version, page tree, media boxes, content operators, extracted text and normative metadata. Object numbers, cross-reference offsets, dictionary order, compression choices, timestamps and document ids are not normative.
Raster images compared by dimensions, colour model, bit depth and decoded samples. Filter selection, interlacing, chunk order, compression level, gamma and ancillary metadata are encoder freedom.
Archives compared as a SET of members by name, uncompressed size and content digest. Entry order, compression method and level, timestamps, attributes and the extra field are writer freedom.
Tables compared by header and cell grid. Line terminator, quote style and trailing newline are writer freedom.
PCM audio compared by format block and decoded samples. Chunk padding, LIST/INFO metadata, chunk order and total byte length are writer freedom.
Meshes compared by vertex set, face topology and counts. Generator strings, comments, precision and solid naming are writer freedom.
